description: JVM nullable slice conformance (ISSUE-0108). Fixtures that run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → the REAL javac compiler frontend (single-module fixtures in-process via compileWithJavac; whole-project fixtures keep the javac launcher) → java subprocess executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: T | null for the four primitives and local classes in locals, module fields, class fields, parameters, and returns; null-check branches (narrowing both directions, else-branch narrowing, narrowing invalidation after assignment, narrowed module fields); nullable boundary checks at the table-read untyped boundary (int | null, class | null nominal checks, array | null); nullable arrays T[] | null; arrays of nullable elements (T | null)[] for the primitives and local classes; class arrays C[] and (C | null)[]; the int()/number() nullable conversion overloads with the runtime null failure; the null-typed inline assignment materialization pins ((m = null) as a nullable-comparison operand, a call argument, the null === null operand, and a class-construction provided value whose sibling hoists a null-typed call — the temporary must be typed java.lang.Object, never java.lang.Void, or javac rejects the artifact after the CLI reported success); and frontend compile-error gates (E3001 nullable-to-non-nullable read, E3001 narrowing invalidation, E3006 int === null) rejected before any backend runs.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-int-locals-flow
tests.description: int | null locals wrap a plain int, hold null, narrow to int in the !== null branch and to null in the === null branch; narrowed arithmetic computes 5+1+1=7

tests.name: jvm-nullable-string-flow
tests.description: string | null narrows to string for concatenation and string equality inside the null-check branch

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boolean-flow
tests.description: boolean | null narrows to boolean in the non-null branch (used as an if condition) and to null in the === null branch

tests.name: jvm-nullable-number-flow
tests.description: number | null flows through a nullable return value, narrows, and feeds number arithmetic

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-flow
tests.description: a local class value wraps into C | null, the null-check branch narrows to C for field reads, and the === null branch holds the null side

tests.name: jvm-nullable-fields
tests.description: required-present nullable fields (int | null, string | null, boolean | null, C | null) default to null, accept writes of values and null, and narrow through locals for reads (1 + 10 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 5 = 23)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-params-returns
tests.description: nullable parameters accept plain values and null; nullable returns carry values and null (0-when returns null, 42 otherwise; want returns 'ok'/null)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-array-local
tests.description: int[] | null holds an array or null; the non-null branch reads, appends via the i === length write, and reads .length; the null side compares === null (1+2+9+4+1=17)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-elements-array
tests.description: (int | null)[] stores null and int elements, reads back null and values with the === null / !== null branches, and reads past the end as the DEAL null (1 + 5 + 1 = 7)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-string-elements-array
tests.description: (string | null)[] literal from homogeneous nullable parameter values, nullable string read, and === null branch on the past-end read

tests.name: jvm-nullable-number-elements-array
tests.description: (number | null)[] writes number and null elements; narrowed reads feed number arithmetic and the int() conversion (5.0 + 1.0 = 6)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boolean-elements-array
tests.description: (boolean | null)[] stores true and null; the === null read branches and the narrowed boolean feeds an if condition

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-arrays
tests.description: C[] holds local class instances with per-class nominal reads/writes; C[] | null narrows to the array; (C | null)[] stores instances and null and narrows reads (1+1+2+1+1+1=7)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-success
tests.description: a table read into an int | null contextual target passes a stored int through the nullable boundary check and narrows (41 + 1 = 42)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-null
tests.description: a table read into an int | null contextual target passes the stored Java-null-equivalent missing entry through as the DEAL null and the === null branch runs

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-failure
tests.description: a table read into an int | null contextual target fails the runtime nullable boundary with E8001 when the stored value is a string (LuaJIT's check_nullable → check_int failure)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-boundary-success
tests.description: a table read into a C | null contextual target runs the nullable nominal check and passes a genuine instance through (x + 1 = 8)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-boundary-failure
tests.description: a table read into a C | null contextual target fails the nullable nominal check with E8001 when the stored value is a plain table (LuaJIT's check_type class branch)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-array-boundary-success
tests.description: a table read into an int[] | null contextual target passes a stored array through the nullable array boundary and narrows to reads (1 + 2 = 3)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-array-boundary-failure
tests.description: a table read into an int[] | null contextual target fails the nullable array boundary with E8001 when the stored value is a table (LuaJIT's check_array failure)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-conversion-intrinsics
tests.description: int(n: int | null) unwraps a present value and number(n: number | null) converts; the results compose (3 + 2 = 5)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-conversion-null-failure
tests.description: int(null-typed int | null) fails at runtime with E8001 'cannot convert null to int' (LuaJIT's int_convert null rejection)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-module-field-narrowing
tests.description: a module-level int | null field narrows inside a function's null-check branch and the doubled value returns (4 * 2 = 8)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-if-else-branches
tests.description: the === null branch narrows to null and the else branch narrows to int; r = 1 on the null side and 0 elsewhere (n starts null)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-typed-flow
tests.description: a null-typed local holds a nullable narrowed-to-null read, and null-typed values compare === null inside a nullable branch

tests.name: jvm-nullable-narrowing-invalidation
tests.description: assigning null inside a narrowed block invalidates the narrowing: the follow-up non-null read is a compile-time E3001 rejected before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-nullable-unwrapped-read-compile-error
tests.description: reading an int | null into an int target without narrowing is a compile-time E3001 rejected before any backend runs

let n: int | null = 1;
let i: int = n;

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-compare-compile-error
tests.description: comparing a plain int with null is a compile-time E3006 rejected before any backend runs (only T | null compares with null)

let b: boolean = i === null;

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-assignment-flow
tests.description: a null-typed assignment expression (whose emitted Java code carries the boxed target's type) flows into int | null, string | null, and null targets, and through a nullable parameter (1 + 10 + 100 + 1 = 112)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-array-wrong-wrapper-boundary
tests.description: a string[] stored in a table and read back as int[] | null fails the wrapper gate with E8001 (the JVM storage analog of LuaJIT's check_array element mismatch) — never a raw cast

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-array-wrong-class-boundary
tests.description: an Other[] stored in a table and read back as Item[] | null fails the per-class wrapper gate with E8001 — the nominal array identity never accepts a same-shaped foreign class array

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-array-boundary-success
tests.description: an Item[] stored in a table and read back as Item[] | null passes the per-class wrapper gate and narrows to reads (x + length = 2)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-declared-locals-flow
tests.description: A binding DECLARED null (let z: null) reads back as the DEAL null into every primitive nullable target: int | null, string | null, boolean | null, and number | null each observe the null side (1+2+4+8=15) — the emitted bare null literal, never the Void-typed name (the pre-fix artifact emitted java.lang.Long m = z; and javac rejected it after the CLI reported success)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-declared-params-module-fields
tests.description: Null-typed values flow into nullable positions from every binding shape: a null-declared local feeds a nullable call argument (take(z)), a nullable class-field write (h.i = z), and a nullable-array element write (ys[0] = z on (int | null)[]); a null-declared MODULE field reads into a nullable local (zmod); and a null-typed PARAMETER returns through a nullable return (ret(z)) — every site observes the null side (1+2+4+8+16=31). The pre-fix artifacts were rejected by javac with incompatible types: Void cannot be converted to Long at each site after the CLI reported success

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-declared-class-array-targets
tests.description: A null-declared local flows into reference nullable targets: a local class target (Holder | null) and an array target (int[] | null) both observe the null side (1+2=3) — the null literal coerces to the generated class reference and the emitted array wrapper reference at the declaration boundary

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-number-accepts-int
tests.description: The table-read nullable boundary is check_nullable for numbers: an int value (stored as java.lang.Long) crossing into number | null passes and computes 6, exactly like runtime.lua's check_number accepting every Lua number (the pre-fix instanceof-only helper raised E8001 'expected number, got Long' where LuaJIT succeeded)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-int-accepts-integral-number
tests.description: The table-read nullable boundary is check_nullable for ints: an integral double value (2.0, stored as java.lang.Double) crossing into int | null passes and computes 3, exactly like runtime.lua's check_int accepting an integral in-range Lua number (the pre-fix instanceof-only helper raised E8001 'expected int, got Double' where LuaJIT succeeded)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-int-nonintegral-failure
tests.description: check_int parity for the int | null table-read boundary: a non-integral number (2.5) raises E8001 'expected int, got non-integer number' (runtime.lua's check_int), exit 1

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-int-nan-failure
tests.description: check_int parity for the int | null table-read boundary: NaN (0.0 / 0.0) raises E8001 'expected int, got NaN' (runtime.lua's check_int), exit 1

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-number-string-failure
tests.description: check_number parity for the number | null table-read boundary: a string value raises E8001 'expected number, got String' (runtime.lua's check_number), exit 1

tests.name: jvm-nullable-boundary-int-range-failure
tests.description: check_int parity for the int | null table-read boundary: an integral number beyond the int safe range (2^53 = 9007199254740992.0) raises E8004 'int out of safe range' (runtime.lua's check_int routes out-of-range values through the emitted checkInt bound), exit 1

tests.name: jvm-nullable-imported-boolean-field-boundary
tests.description: A nil-capable boolean value (&& over a past-end boolean[] read) written to an IMPORTED class's boolean field crosses the field's typed boundary and raises E8001 'expected boolean, got null' (LuaJIT's check_boolean at the write), exit 1 — the member-assign boundary falls back to the value's type when the field's declared type is unresolvable across modules, exactly like the identifier-assignment fallback (the pre-fix emission assigned the boxed Boolean temp straight to the primitive field and raised a raw java.lang.NullPointerException)

modules.lib.deal: export class Box { flag: boolean = false; }

tests.name: jvm-nullable-imported-boolean-field-in-bounds
tests.description: Positive control for the imported-class member-assign boundary: an in-bounds nil-aware value (xs[0] || xs[1] = true) writes into the imported boolean field and reads back as true (7) — the fallback boundary never over-rejects a non-null value

modules.lib.deal: export class Box { flag: boolean = false; }

tests.name: jvm-nullable-comparison-once-eval-eq
tests.description: T | null === T | null evaluates each inline effectful operand exactly once in strict left-to-right order: mark('l',1) prints l, mark('r',2) prints r, and the differing values compare false (8) — the contiguous trace l,r,8 forbids the pre-fix double evaluation (the pre-fix ternary referenced each operand twice and printed l,r,l,r)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-comparison-once-eval-neq
tests.description: T | null !== T | null evaluates each inline effectful operand exactly once in strict left-to-right order: mark('l',1) prints l, mark('r',1) prints r, and the equal values compare !== false (8) — the contiguous trace pins the NEQ ternary's materialization the same way the EQ shape pins the equality form

tests.name: jvm-nullable-comparison-null-side-once
tests.description: T | null === null evaluates the nullable operand once (l prints exactly once) and compares false (8) — the materialized left operand is never double-evaluated

tests.name: jvm-nullable-comparison-null-side-order
tests.description: T | null === null keeps strict left-to-right order when the null side is a side-effecting null-typed call: mark('l',1) prints l before touch('r') prints r, then the comparison is false (8) — the left operand is materialized before the right operand's evaluation (the pre-fix lowering evaluated the materialized right operand before the inline left operand)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-assign-comparison-materialize
tests.description: A null-typed inline assignment ((m = null), m: int | null — the emitted code carries the boxed assignment target's Java type Long) as the left operand of the null === T | null comparison, followed by an operand that hoists a null-typed call (pick(2, log('x'))): the operand materialization must type the temporary java.lang.Object, never javaLocalType(null) = java.lang.Void — the pre-fix emitted java.lang.Void __t0 = (m = null); and javac rejected the artifact with 'incompatible types: Long cannot be converted to Void' after the CLI reported success. The artifact is javac-valid, log('x') prints x exactly once (once-evaluation), and null === 2 compares false

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-assign-call-arg-materialize
tests.description: A null-typed inline assignment as a call argument preceding a hoisting argument: f((m = null), pick(2, log('x'))) — the argument materialization must type the temporary java.lang.Object (the pre-fix emitted java.lang.Void __t0 = (m = null);, rejected by javac with 'incompatible types: Long cannot be converted to Void' after the CLI reported success). f receives the DEAL null and returns the second argument: x then 2

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-assign-null-equality-materialize
tests.description: The null === null comparison branch with a null-typed inline assignment against a hoisting null-typed call: (m = null) === touch('r') — the materialized assignment temporary must be java.lang.Object (the pre-fix emitted java.lang.Void __t0 = (m = null);, rejected by javac). touch prints r once, then null === null compares true

tests.name: jvm-nullable-null-assign-class-ctor-value
tests.description: A null-typed inline assignment as a provided class-construction value for a nullable field: { y: (m = null) } with y: int | null — the provided-value materialization must type the temporary java.lang.Object (the pre-fix emitted java.lang.Void __t0 = (m = null);, rejected by javac after the CLI reported success) and the constructor's nullable parameter accepts the DEAL null (p.y === null reads back true → 7)

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-nullable-target-primitives
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for past-end reads of non-nullable primitive element arrays at a T | null target: the spec's read-site contract (spec-v1.2 §Bounds and nil behavior — 'Optional nullable arrays follow target typing') checks the read result against the TARGET type, so LuaJIT's check_nullable accepts the nil and the JVM read must yield the DEAL null instead of raising the element-typed E8001. The in-bounds positive control pins value preservation (20 / a / true / 1.5) through the same nullable declarations.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-nullable-target-class
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for a past-end read of a local-class array at a C | null target: LuaJIT's check_nullable accepts the nil (Point | null receives the DEAL null) and the JVM read must yield the DEAL null through the per-class nullable read instead of raising E8001 'expected instance of Point, got null' at the element-typed read. The in-bounds positive control pins the nominal value preservation (q2.x === 5).

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-comparison-class-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for local-class array reads in === / !== operand positions: the comparison operand applies no typed boundary (spec-v1.2 §Bounds and nil behavior), so ps[9] === ps[9] is nil === nil (true), p === ps[9] and ps[9] === p are value-vs-nil (false), and p !== ps[9] / ps[9] !== p are true — the JVM must emit the nil-yielding per-class read exactly like the primitive boxed comparison reads, never the element-typed E8001 read. The in-bounds positive controls pin nominal identity (ps[0] === ps[0] and p === ps[0] are the same instance).

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-boundary-positions
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for the read-site target typing at every typed boundary position: a past-end int[] read consumed by a nullable assignment RHS, a nullable call argument, a nullable class-field write, a (int | null)[] element write, a nullable class-construction value, and a nullable function return all yield the DEAL null exactly where LuaJIT's per-position check_nullable accepts the nil. The in-bounds positive control pins value preservation.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-nonnullable-target-still-e8001
tests.description: Positive control for the consume-aware read: a past-end int[] read at a NON-nullable int target still raises E8001 'expected int, got null' on both backends (LuaJIT's check_int(nil) at the declaration boundary; the JVM's element-typed read) — the nullable-target yield must never leak into non-nullable boundary positions.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-nonnullable-class-target-e8001
tests.description: Positive control for the consume-aware read on class arrays: a past-end Point[] read at a NON-nullable Point target still raises E8001 on both backends (LuaJIT's check_type class branch fails on the nil; the JVM's per-class element-typed read) — the nullable-target yield must never leak into non-nullable class boundary positions.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-arr-gate-accepts-plain-int
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for the (int | null)[] table-read gate accepting a plain int[] value: LuaJIT's check_nullable over the (int | null)[] descriptor validates every element with check_nullable(int) — every plain int passes — so the stored int[] reads back into (int | null)[] and computes 10+20+30 with length 3. The pre-fix JVM gate was instanceof-only and raised E8001 'expected array, got __IntArray' where the reference succeeds.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-arr-gate-accepts-plain-multi
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for the number[]/string[]/boolean[] table-read gates accepting plain element arrays at (T | null)[] targets: LuaJIT's check_array validates each element against check_nullable(T) and every plain T element passes, so all three stored arrays read back and verify their values. The pre-fix JVM gates raised E8001 'expected array, got __NumberArray/__StringArray/__BooleanArray' where the reference succeeds.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-arr-gate-accepts-plain
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for the (C | null)[] table-read gate accepting a plain C[] value: LuaJIT's check_array validates each element against check_nullable(C) and a plain C element passes, so the stored Item[] reads back into (Item | null)[] and its element keeps its nominal value (v === 7). The pre-fix JVM shared one wrapper/gate for C[] and (C | null)[] with an instanceof-only gate.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-arr-or-null-rejected-luajit
tests.description: LuaJIT reference pin: a (C | null)[] containing a null crossing a C[]-typed table-read boundary fails the boundary read with E8003 'array element 1 type mismatch' (check_array validates each element against the non-nullable C descriptor and the null fails), exit 1 — the JVM side of the same program is pinned by jvm-nullable-class-arr-or-null-rejected-jvm (E8001, the documented storage-analog code-number divergence).

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-arr-or-null-rejected-jvm
tests.description: JVM pin: a (C | null)[] containing a null crossing a C[]-typed table-read boundary fails the boundary gate with E8001 'expected array, got …' (the distinct $ArrayOrNull$<C> wrapper never passes the C[] $Array$<C> gate, so the null element can never cross the typed boundary unvalidated), exit 1 — the pre-fix JVM shared one wrapper for C[] and (C | null)[] and silently let the null-containing array through. The LuaJIT reference side of the same program raises E8003 (pinned by jvm-nullable-class-arr-or-null-rejected-luajit; the E8001-vs-E8003 code-number difference is the documented storage-analog divergence).

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-nullable-arg-materialize
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for a nil-yielding nullable-target read materialized ahead of a hoisting sibling argument: take(xs[9], pick(2, log('x'))) — the past-end read at the int | null parameter yields the DEAL null, and the emitOperandsInOrder materialization must type the read's temporary with the BOXED element type (java.lang.Long for the emitted __intArrayReadBoxed code, never the long storage type — javac rejects 'long __t0 = __intArrayReadBoxed(...)'). The hoisted 'x' print stays after the read's evaluation and before pick runs, so the trace is x, picked, null-arg.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-module-level
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for load-time (module-level) declarations consuming past-end reads at T | null targets: the static-initializer path must carry the same nil-yielding read — a direct read (n) and a read materialized ahead of a hoisting sibling argument (m, whose 'm' print hoists into the static block) both receive the DEAL null at load time, so the single zero-arity export observes both.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-read-class-nullable-arg-materialize
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for a LOCAL-CLASS nil-yielding nullable-target read materialized ahead of a hoisting sibling argument: take(ps[9], pick(2, log('x'))) with the first parameter Point | null — the per-class nullable read yields the DEAL null past the end, and the emitOperandsInOrder materialization types the read's temporary with the generated class reference (the emitted $classOrNullArrayRead$<Point> code's Java type). The hoisted 'x' print stays after the read's evaluation and before pick runs: x, picked, null-arg.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-or-null-class-read-comparisons
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for (C | null)[] element reads in === / !== positions: the or-null read yields the DEAL null past the end and for a stored null, so mp[9] === null and mp[1] === null are true, mp[0] === mp[0] is nominal identity (true), and mp[9] === mp[9] is nil === nil (true) — the nullable-typed operands route through the nullable comparison lowering with the once-evaluated boxed values.

tests.name: jvm-nullable-class-arr-or-null-roundtrip
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for a (C | null)[] stored in a table and read back at the SAME (C | null)[] target: the or-null wrapper's own gate passes it through unchanged (the distinct $ArrayOrNull$<C> wrapper round-trips), the stored null element stays null and the stored instance keeps its nominal value (v === 7) — the positive control for the wrapper split that makes the C[] gate reject null-containing arrays.
